newsitem.title: FRANCE: French union leader warns against more austerity.
newsitem.headline: French union leader warns against more austerity.

text.p: Louis Viannet, leader of France's Communist-dominated CGT trade union, warned on Thursday that a government move towards new austerity measures this autumn would lead to serious labour unrest.
If worries over the state of France's public finances were to lead to "a new turn of the screw this autumn, we would see a very strong clash," Viannet told the French daily Liberation.
France's new leftist government came to power in a June 1 parliamentary election pledging an end to austerity to help France qualify for European economic and monetary union from 1999.

But after taking over the government, Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin ordered an audit of public finances amidst grim warnings that public deficits may be higher than expected and above the level required for a move to the euro.
Viannet, noting the government murmurings about the condition of state finances, warned that the new leftist majority "was carried to power so it could go in a new direction".

The upset defeat of the previous centre-right majority has been widely blamed on the public spending cuts, civil servant wage freezes and reductions in public service and welfare programmes that it argued were needed to shift to the single European currency.
"The country has no need today of additional cuts in useful spending," Viannet said. "On the contrary, we must ease the constraints weighing on economic activity and growth."
He said moves in this direction would help ease France's stubborn and politically troubling 12.8 percent unemployment rate.

Viannet faulted Jospin for his silence on wage expectations for civil servants, saying his failure to enunciate a policy on eagerly anticipated salary hikes was "creating genuine discontent" among public workers.
